methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $100M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Ocean Infinity, a Growth-stage company in the Ocean & Maritime sector founded by Oliver Plunkett, has raised $100M+ to date. The comparable universe is limited, consisting of one identifiable private peer (Orbital Marine Power) and no public comps, reflecting the nascent nature of frontier maritime technology.

Given the sparse comp set, valuation relies on stage-progression methodology. Using total capital raised ($100M) as a baseline proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of Growth-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $120M. This single-method triangulation produces a range anchored at $102M (low), $120M (median), and $138M (high), derived from sensitivity around the stage multiplier assumption.

The $120M median valuation is defensible as a near-term fair value but carries material uncertainty. The analysis is constrained by a single applicable method and an extremely limited peer set, precluding meaningful cross-sector or multiple-based validation. Key risks to valuation include actual revenue, margin profile, and capital efficiency relative to peers—none of which are present in available data. A more robust assessment would require operational metrics, comparable transaction multiples, or expansion of the peer universe beyond the single identified private reference.
